394	   230	    /// Everything a caption run will do, computed against `project` and
395	   231	    /// applied by nobody: the UI commits it through `ProjectDocument`, the
396	   232	    /// agent through `AgentServer.editResult`.
397	   233	    ///
398	   234	    /// `existing` is whatever the producer already refused — a malformed SubRip
399	   235	    /// block, an ineligible clip — and rides along so one report carries both
400	   236	    /// halves.
401	   237	    ///
402	   238	    /// `track` places on an existing track; absent, the captions get a new
403	   239	    /// front-most track of their own, which is the only placement that can
404	   240	    /// never be refused by the overlap rule.
405	   241	    ///
406	   242	    /// `style` is the caption style (road map 8's W4a). `.subtitles` is the
407	   243	    /// Caption preset and the code path this function always had, byte for
408	   244	    /// byte for a cue with no speaker; a speaker's cue adds its palette
409	   245	    /// `color` (`CaptionStyle.speakerColors`, spec §11 R6-22). A word
410	   246	    /// style writes `style.pagePatch` per page — the props the pager measured,
411	   247	    /// at the page's own size (a shrunk one or the style's), with its wrap
412	   248	    /// width and its `words` in CLIP time — and puts the batch at the style's
413	   249	    /// `y`, with the run's `looks` (W-15). `replacing` names caption tracks to remove
414	   250	    /// WITH their clips in the same ops, first — `replaceableTracks` says
415	   251	    /// which qualify — and the new track takes their place at the front.
416	   252	    static func place(
417	   253	        _ cues: [Cue], problems existing: [Problem] = [], in project: ReelProject,
418	   254	        track: UInt32? = nil, trackBase: String = "Captions", style: CaptionStyle = .subtitles,
419	   255	        looks: CaptionLooks = .none, replacing: [UInt32] = []
420	   256	    ) throws -> Plan {
421	   257	        let snapshot = project.snapshot
422	   258	        let canvas = snapshot.canvas
423	   259	        let frame = max(canvas.fps.frameDuration, 1)
424	   260	        guard !cues.isEmpty else { throw LayoutError.noCues(existing) }
425	   261	
426	   262	        // Snap, then give a cue that snapped to nothing its one frame back,
427	   263	        // THEN resolve overlaps — in that order, so an overlap the minimum
428	   264	        // length introduces is still one the overlap pass fixes.
429	   265	        var placed = cues.enumerated().map { index, cue -> Placed in
430	   266	            let start = ReelTime.snapToFrame(max(0, cue.start), fps: canvas.fps)
431	   267	            let end = ReelTime.snapToFrame(cue.end, fps: canvas.fps)
432	   268	            return Placed(
433	   269	                tag: cue.tag, order: index, start: start, end: max(end, start + frame),
434	   270	                text: cue.text, words: cue.words, size: cue.size, width: cue.width,
435	   271	                speaker: cue.speaker)
436	   272	        }
437	   273	        placed.sort { $0.start == $1.start ? $0.order < $1.order : $0.start < $1.start }
438	   274	
439	   275	        // Captions are one track, so two cues on screen at once cannot both
440	   276	        // be honoured: the later one wins its start and the earlier one is
441	   277	        // cut back to it. That is also what the overlap rule (§6) would
442	   278	        // otherwise refuse the placement over.
443	   279	        var trimmed = 0
444	   280	        for index in placed.indices.dropLast() where placed[index].end > placed[index + 1].start {
445	   281	            placed[index].end = placed[index + 1].start
446	   282	            trimmed += 1
447	   283	        }
448	   284	        var problems = existing
449	   285	        for cue in placed where cue.end - cue.start < frame {
450	   286	            problems.append(
451	   287	                Problem(tag: cue.tag, reason: "starts less than a frame before the next caption"))
452	   288	        }
453	   289	        let kept = placed.filter { $0.end - $0.start >= frame }
454	   290	        guard !kept.isEmpty else { throw LayoutError.noCues(problems) }
455	   291	
456	   292	        // Before a single op: every op runs `Project::validate`, so a
457	   293	        // transcript one clip too long would throw about clips, halfway
458	   294	        // through, with the earlier ones already applied purely and thrown
459	   295	        // away. The count is known here.
460	   296	        let removed = Set(replacing)
461	   297	        let room = Int(RC_MAX_CLIPS) - snapshot.clips.filter { !removed.contains($0.track) }.count
462	   298	        guard kept.count <= room else {
463	   299	            throw LayoutError.tooMany(cues: kept.count, room: max(0, room))
464	   300	        }
465	   301	
466	   302	        // The replaced tracks go FIRST, clips and all: a removal mints no
467	   303	        // id, so `next_id` below is still the new track's, and the new
468	   304	        // track's index counts the stack as it will be once they are gone.
469	   305	        var ops: [ReelOp] = replacing.map { .removeTrack(track: $0, withClips: true) }
470	   306	        let destination: UInt32
471	   307	        let name = trackName(in: snapshot, base: trackBase, excluding: replacing)
472	   308	        if let track = track {
473	   309	            destination = track
474	   310	        } else {
475	   311	            // A new id is `next_id` from BEFORE the op — the documented
476	   312	            // contract of the one JSON entry point (§6), since an op returns
477	   313	            // a project rather than an id. Index `tracks.count` is the front
478	   314	            // of the stack, so captions draw over everything.
479	   315	            destination = snapshot.nextId
480	   316	            ops.append(.addTrack(index: snapshot.tracks.count - replacing.count, name: name))
481	   317	        }
482	   318	
483	   319	        let preset = captionPreset
484	   320	        let height = Double(canvas.height)
485	   321	        let size = CGSize(width: canvas.width, height: canvas.height)
486	   322	        var overTwoLines = 0
487	   323	        if style.isWordStyle {
488	   324	            let base = style.size(for: CGSize(width: canvas.width, height: canvas.height))
489	   325	            for cue in kept {
490	   326	                let words = cue.words.map { words in
491	   327	                    words.map { TextWord(start: $0.start - cue.start, end: $0.end - cue.start) }
492	   328	                }
493	   329	                ops.append(
494	   330	                    .addTextClip(
495	   331	                        track: destination, at: cue.start, duration: cue.end - cue.start,
496	   332	                        text: style.pagePatch(
497	   333	                            content: cue.text, size: cue.size ?? base, width: cue.width,
498	   334	                            words: words, looks: looks)))
499	   335	            }
500	   336	        } else {
501	   337	            var base = TextPatch(
502	   338	                font: preset.font, size: preset.size(on: size),
503	   339	                align: preset.align, valign: "middle", backdrop: .some(preset.backdrop),
504	   340	                width: .some(Double(canvas.width) * wrapFraction))
505	   341	            if canvas.height > canvas.width {
506	   342	                overTwoLines = kept.filter { measuresOverTwoLines($0.text, preset, on: size) }
507	   343	                    .count
508	   344	            }
509	   345	            let colors = CaptionStyle.speakerColors(kept.map(\.speaker))
510	   346	            for (cue, color) in zip(kept, colors) {
511	   347	                base.content = cue.text
512	   348	                base.color = color
513	   349	                ops.append(
514	   350	                    .addTextClip(
515	   351	                        track: destination, at: cue.start, duration: cue.end - cue.start,
516	   352	                        text: base))
517	   353	            }
518	   354	        }
519	   355	
520	   356	        // The preset's position is a `set_video` patch, and a patch needs
521	   357	        // ids the ops have not minted yet — so the batch is applied PURELY
522	   358	        // first and the ids read off the throwaway result. Applying the same
523	   359	        // ops to the same handle mints the same ids, which is what makes
524	   360	        // appending the patch to this very list correct
525	   361	        // (`EditorViewController+AddClips.swift` does the same for one clip).
526	   362	        //
527	   363	        // The probe is kept rather than replaced by arithmetic on `next_id`:
528	   364	        // ids ARE sequential when nothing is refused, and that is exactly the
529	   365	        // invariant a refusal breaks — a caller-named track can refuse any
530	   366	        // number of these placements, and then the patch would name clips
531	   367	        // that do not exist.
532	   368	        guard let probed = try project.applying(ops).project else { throw LayoutError.refused }
533	   369	        let before = Set(snapshot.clips.map { $0.id })
534	   370	        let created = probed.snapshot.clips.map { $0.id }.filter { !before.contains($0) }
535	   371	        guard !created.isEmpty else { throw LayoutError.refused }
536	   372	        let at = preset.position(on: size)
537	   373	        ops.append(
538	   374	            .setVideo(
539	   375	                clips: created,
540	   376	                patch: style.isWordStyle
541	   377	                    ? VideoPatch(x: 0, y: style.yFraction * height)
542	   378	                    : VideoPatch(x: at.x, y: at.y, opacity: 1)))
543	   379	
544	   380	        return Plan(
545	   381	            ops: ops, clips: created.count, cues: kept.count, trimmed: trimmed,
546	   382	            problems: problems, trackName: track == nil ? name : nil, replaced: replacing,
547	   383	            overTwoLines: overTwoLines)
548	   384	    }

550	   386	    /// Whether a Subtitles cue, as `place` writes it on `canvas` (the Caption preset, its
551	   387	    /// wrap box), measures taller than the same props holding two lines (spec §11 VR-41).
552	   388	    static func measuresOverTwoLines(
553	   389	        _ content: String, _ preset: TextPreset, on canvas: CGSize
554	   390	    ) -> Bool {
555	   391	        func props(_ text: String) -> TextProps {
556	   392	            TextProps(
557	   393	                content: text, font: preset.font, size: preset.size(on: canvas),
558	   394	                align: preset.align, valign: "middle", backdrop: preset.backdrop,
559	   395	                width: Double(canvas.width) * wrapFraction)
560	   396	        }
561	   397	        return LayerRenderers.measuredSize(for: props(content)).height
562	   398	            > LayerRenderers.measuredSize(for: props("X\nX")).height
563	   399	    }

565	   401	    /// The tracks a restyle may replace (road map 8 §5e's three rules): a
566	   402	    /// track named as this file names caption tracks ("Captions",
567	   403	    /// "Captions N"), holding at least one clip and only text clips, each overlapping
568	   404	    /// some job's `span` — so nothing outside the run's scope is removed.
569	   405	    static func replaceableTracks(
570	   406	        in snapshot: ProjectSnapshot, jobs: [Transcriber.Job]
571	   407	    ) -> [UInt32] {
572	   408	        snapshot.tracks.compactMap { track -> UInt32? in
573	   409	            guard isCaptionTrackName(track.name) else { return nil }
574	   410	            guard snapshot.clips.contains(where: { $0.track == track.id }) else { return nil }
575	   411	            for clip in snapshot.clips where clip.track == track.id {
576	   412	                guard case .text = clip.source else { return nil }
577	   413	                let end = clip.start + clip.duration
578	   414	                guard jobs.contains(where: { $0.span.overlaps(clip.start ..< end) }) else {
579	   415	                    return nil
580	   416	                }
581	   417	            }
582	   418	            return track.id
583	   419	        }
584	   420	    }
585	   421	
586	   422	    /// A name this file gives a caption track: "Captions" or "Captions N".
587	   423	    static func isCaptionTrackName(_ name: String) -> Bool {
588	   424	        if name == "Captions" { return true }
589	   425	        guard name.hasPrefix("Captions ") else { return false }
590	   426	        let suffix = name.dropFirst("Captions ".count)
591	   427	        return !suffix.isEmpty && suffix.allSatisfy { $0.isASCII && $0.isNumber }
592	   428	    }
593	   429	
594	   430	    /// "Captions", then "Captions 2" — so two runs are tellable apart in the
595	   431	    /// track header. `base` is the producer's word for what it made, and both
596	   432	    /// producers say "Captions": a transcript and an imported file are the
597	   433	    /// same thing on the timeline, and a second name would only make the
598	   434	    /// numbering restart.
599	   435	    /// A track in `excluding` is one this plan removes, so its name is free.
600	   436	    static func trackName(
601	   437	        in snapshot: ProjectSnapshot, base: String = "Captions", excluding: [UInt32] = []
602	   438	    ) -> String {
603	   439	        let taken = Set(snapshot.tracks.filter { !excluding.contains($0.id) }.map { $0.name })
604	   440	        var name = base
605	   441	        var suffix = 2
606	   442	        while taken.contains(name) {
607	   443	            name = "\(base) \(suffix)"
608	   444	            suffix += 1
609	   445	        }
610	   446	        return name
611	   447	    }

226	   226	    static func previewReveals(tokens: Int, looks: CaptionLooks) -> [RecipeReveal] {
227	   227	        let fill = looks.fill ? previewFill : nil
228	   228	        let glide = looks.slide && tokens >= 2 ? previewGlide : nil
229	   229	        return [
230	   230	            RecipeReveal(word: 1, wordPop: 1, wordFill: fill),

235	   235	    /// The sample page drawn by the renderer: two frames for a word style
236	   236	    /// (`previewReveals`), one for Subtitles, each
237	   237	    /// scaled to fit a 258×36 slot, stacked 8 pt apart over the plate, at 2×.
238	   238	    func preview() -> NSImage? {
239	   239	        let canvas = CGSize(width: snapshot.canvas.width, height: snapshot.canvas.height)
240	   240	        let frame = max(snapshot.canvas.fps.frameDuration, 1)
241	   241	        guard
242	   242	            let cue = CaptionPages.samplePage(
243	   243	                sampleWords(), request: pagesRequest, frame: frame)
244	   244	        else { return nil }
245	   245	        let props = previewProps(for: cue, canvas: canvas)
246	   246	        let reveals =
247	   247	            style.isWordStyle
248	   248	            ? Self.previewReveals(tokens: props.tokenCount, looks: looks)
249	   249	            : [RecipeReveal.whole]
250	   250	        let size = Self.previewSize
251	   251	        let scale: CGFloat = 2
252	   252	        guard
253	   253	            let context = LayerRenderers.bitmap(
254	   254	                CGSize(width: size.width * scale, height: size.height * scale))
255	   255	        else { return nil }
256	   256	        context.setFillColor(DS.captionPreviewPlate.cgColor)
257	   257	        context.fill(CGRect(x: 0, y: 0, width: context.width, height: context.height))
258	   258	        context.scaleBy(x: scale, y: scale)
259	   259	        context.interpolationQuality = .high
260	   260	
261	   261	        let slot = CGSize(width: size.width, height: 36)
262	   262	        let gap: CGFloat = 8
263	   263	        let count = CGFloat(reveals.count)
264	   264	        // From the TOP, in points; the context is y-up.
265	   265	        var top = (size.height - count * slot.height - (count - 1) * gap) / 2
266	   266	        for reveal in reveals {
267	   267	            if let bitmap = LayerRenderers.textBitmap(props, reveal: reveal),
268	   268	                let image = bitmap.makeImage()
269	   269	            {
270	   270	                let fit = min(
271	   271	                    slot.width / CGFloat(image.width), slot.height / CGFloat(image.height))
272	   272	                let drawn = CGSize(
273	   273	                    width: CGFloat(image.width) * fit, height: CGFloat(image.height) * fit)
274	   274	                context.draw(
275	   275	                    image,
276	   276	                    in: CGRect(
277	   277	                        x: (size.width - drawn.width) / 2,
278	   278	                        y: size.height - top - slot.height + (slot.height - drawn.height) / 2,
279	   279	                        width: drawn.width, height: drawn.height))
280	   280	            }
281	   281	            top += slot.height + gap
282	   282	        }
283	   283	        guard let image = context.makeImage() else { return nil }
284	   284	        return NSImage(cgImage: image, size: size)
285	   285	    }

565	   401	    /// The tracks a restyle may replace (road map 8 §5e's three rules): a

567	   403	    /// "Captions N"), holding at least one clip and only text clips, each overlapping
568	   404	    /// some job's `span` — so nothing outside the run's scope is removed.

571	   407	    ) -> [UInt32] {

573	   409	            guard isCaptionTrackName(track.name) else { return nil }
574	   410	            guard snapshot.clips.contains(where: { $0.track == track.id }) else { return nil }

576	   412	                guard case .text = clip.source else { return nil }
577	   413	                let end = clip.start + clip.duration
578	   414	                guard jobs.contains(where: { $0.span.overlaps(clip.start ..< end) }) else {
579	   415	                    return nil
580	   416	                }
581	   417	            }

236	   236	    /// (`previewReveals`), one for Subtitles, each
237	   237	    /// scaled to fit a 258×36 slot, stacked 8 pt apart over the plate, at 2×.
238	   238	    func preview() -> NSImage? {
239	   239	        let canvas = CGSize(width: snapshot.canvas.width, height: snapshot.canvas.height)
240	   240	        let frame = max(snapshot.canvas.fps.frameDuration, 1)
241	   241	        guard
242	   242	            let cue = CaptionPages.samplePage(
243	   243	                sampleWords(), request: pagesRequest, frame: frame)
244	   244	        else { return nil }
245	   245	        let props = previewProps(for: cue, canvas: canvas)
246	   246	        let reveals =
247	   247	            style.isWordStyle
248	   248	            ? Self.previewReveals(tokens: props.tokenCount, looks: looks)
249	   249	            : [RecipeReveal.whole]
250	   250	        let size = Self.previewSize
251	   251	        let scale: CGFloat = 2
252	   252	        guard
253	   253	            let context = LayerRenderers.bitmap(
254	   254	                CGSize(width: size.width * scale, height: size.height * scale))
255	   255	        else { return nil }
256	   256	        context.setFillColor(DS.captionPreviewPlate.cgColor)
257	   257	        context.fill(CGRect(x: 0, y: 0, width: context.width, height: context.height))
258	   258	        context.scaleBy(x: scale, y: scale)
259	   259	        context.interpolationQuality = .high
260	   260	
261	   261	        let slot = CGSize(width: size.width, height: 36)
262	   262	        let gap: CGFloat = 8
263	   263	        let count = CGFloat(reveals.count)
264	   264	        // From the TOP, in points; the context is y-up.
265	   265	        var top = (size.height - count * slot.height - (count - 1) * gap) / 2
266	   266	        for reveal in reveals {
267	   267	            if let bitmap = LayerRenderers.textBitmap(props, reveal: reveal),
268	   268	                let image = bitmap.makeImage()
269	   269	            {
270	   270	                let fit = min(
271	   271	                    slot.width / CGFloat(image.width), slot.height / CGFloat(image.height))
272	   272	                let drawn = CGSize(
273	   273	                    width: CGFloat(image.width) * fit, height: CGFloat(image.height) * fit)
274	   274	                context.draw(
275	   275	                    image,
276	   276	                    in: CGRect(
277	   277	                        x: (size.width - drawn.width) / 2,
278	   278	                        y: size.height - top - slot.height + (slot.height - drawn.height) / 2,
279	   279	                        width: drawn.width, height: drawn.height))
280	   280	            }
281	   281	            top += slot.height + gap
282	   282	        }
283	   283	        guard let image = context.makeImage() else { return nil }
284	   284	        return NSImage(cgImage: image, size: size)
285	   285	    }

293	     7	/// per line under the Style popup and above the preview, and the note about
294	     8	/// on-device pauses under them.
295	     9	///
296	    10	/// **A box that does not apply is greyed, not hidden, and keeps its tick.**
297	    11	/// `refreshLooksRow()` sets each box's `isEnabled` from
298	    12	/// `CaptionLooks.Look.isLive(for:)` and never its state, so Slide ticked on
299	    13	/// Pill is still ticked after a trip through Karaoke; `looks` counts a box
300	    14	/// only while it is ENABLED and on, which is what `finish` hands `place` and
301	    15	/// what the preview draws.
302	    16	///
303	    17	/// **Each box is remembered under its own key**, read when the row is built
304	    18	/// and written by a CLICK (`lookChanged`) — never by Generate — and never by
305	    19	/// the tool (R6-2 read across). An absent key is off, so a build that
306	    20	/// remembered only a style opens with all three off.
307	    21	///
308	    22	/// **The note** shows whenever On this Mac is the engine and Dim is live (a
309	    23	/// word style), ticked or not: the on-device engine's word ranges tile the
310	    24	/// audio, so its words rarely carry the pause a dim waits for (W-13). It
311	    25	/// wraps to two lines at the column's width, so the card is about two lines
312	    26	/// taller while it shows.
313	    27	extension TranscribeSheetController {
314	    28	
315	    29	    /// The owner's sentence (spec §11 W-15).
316	    30	    static let dimNote = "On-device words rarely carry a pause; this shows mostly with AssemblyAI."
317	    31	
318	    32	    /// The looks a run commits: each box ENABLED and on.
319	    33	    var looks: CaptionLooks {
320	    34	        var out = CaptionLooks.none
321	    35	        for look in CaptionLooks.Look.allCases {
322	    36	            let box = checkbox(for: look)
323	    37	            out[look] = box.isEnabled && box.state == .on
324	    38	        }

326	    40	    }

329	    43	        switch look {
330	    44	        case .slide: return slideCheckbox
331	    45	        case .fill: return fillCheckbox
332	    46	        case .dim: return dimCheckbox

334	    48	    }

336	    50	    /// Grid row 8: the three boxes stacked, each opening on its remembered
337	    51	    /// state, and the note. `makeReplaceRow()` is the pattern.
338	    52	    func makeLooksRow() -> [NSView] {
339	    53	        var views: [NSView] = []
340	    54	        for look in CaptionLooks.Look.allCases {
341	    55	            let box = checkbox(for: look)
342	    56	            box.title = look.title
343	    57	            box.font = DS.sans(12)
344	    58	            box.target = self
345	    59	            box.action = #selector(lookChanged(_:))
346	    60	            box.state = defaults.bool(forKey: look.defaultsKey) ? .on : .off
347	    61	            box.setAccessibilityIdentifier("captions.look.\(look.rawValue)")

351	    65	        dimNoteLabel.font = DS.sans(11)

386	     3	// MARK: - Sheet: the commit and the command
387	     4	
388	     5	/// The run's one exit and the menu command that opens the sheet: `finish`,
389	     6	/// the single place all four outcomes land (`summary` is the sentence it
390	     7	/// writes), `viewDidDisappear`, which cancels a
391	     8	/// run the sheet is dismissed out from under, and File ▸ Generate
392	     9	/// Captions… itself with the validator arm that greys it.
393	    10	///
394	    11	/// A pure move out of `TranscribeSheetController.swift`, road map 6's C1
395	    12	/// toll 3. Both blocks came here whole and in their own order, with every
396	    13	/// line byte-identical. One widening in the move — `finish` is internal
397	    14	/// rather than `private`, which the compiler forces, since `begin` stayed
398	    15	/// behind and calls it — and nine in the file it left, the stored
399	    16	/// properties `finish` and `viewDidDisappear` read. `summary` stays
400	    17	/// `private`: only `finish` calls it, and it moved with it. W2 deleted
401	    18	/// `truncationText` with the ceiling it reported (spec §11 W-8).
402	    19	///
403	    20	/// **c1-chrome added the cloud engine's three lines** (road map 6 §5e), and
404	    21	/// it is no longer only a move. `cloudReportLines` turns the run's `Report`
405	    22	/// into what the card says beside today's counts — R6-8's fallback, the
406	    23	/// language that was DETECTED and how sure the service was, and any media
407	    24	/// whose remote delete is still owed. They are added in BOTH arms: a run
408	    25	/// that failed can still have uploaded one media and owe a delete for it,
409	    26	/// and a card that printed only the error would lose the one record a
410	    27	/// person has of that.
411	    28	extension TranscribeSheetController {
412	    29	
413	    30	    // MARK: - Commit
414	    31	
415	    32	    /// The one exit for all four outcomes — finished, finished with something
416	    33	    /// to say, failed and cancelled.
417	    34	    ///
418	    35	    /// The plan is built HERE, against the document's CURRENT handle, not
419	    36	    /// against the snapshot this sheet opened with: recognition is minutes
420	    37	    /// long and an agent can edit a document while a sheet is up, and
421	    38	    /// `CaptionLayout.place` reads ids off a probe of the handle it is given.
422	    39	    /// The commit goes through `performGroupedEdit` because a queue completion
423	    40	    /// is not an AppKit event — the road map says `applyEdit` here, and
424	    41	    /// following it would silently merge the captions into whatever edit came
425	    42	    /// before them (app/CLAUDE.md's undo pitfall).
426	    43	    func finish(_ outcome: Result<Transcriber.Outcome, any Error>) {
427	    44	        guard !didFinish else { return }
428	    45	        didFinish = true
429	    46	        bar.doubleValue = 1
430	    47	        stopButton.title = "Close"
431	    48	        stopButton.isEnabled = true
432	    49	        detailLabel.stringValue = ""
433	    50	
434	    51	        let cloudLines = cloudReport.map {
435	    52	            Self.cloudReportLines($0, names: mediaNames, detected: cloudDetected)
436	    53	        } ?? []
437	    54	        let result: Transcriber.Outcome
438	    55	        switch outcome {
439	    56	        case .failure(let error):
440	    57	            statusLabel.stringValue = ([error.localizedDescription] + cloudLines)
441	    58	                .joined(separator: "\n")
442	    59	            statusLabel.textColor = DS.textStrong
443	    60	            return
444	    61	        case .success(let value):
445	    62	            result = value
446	    63	        }
447	    64	        guard let document = document else {
448	    65	            statusLabel.stringValue = "The project closed before the captions could be placed."
449	    66	            return
450	    67	        }
451	    68	        let plan: CaptionLayout.Plan
452	    69	        do {
453	    70	            let replacing = replaceExisting
454	    71	                ? CaptionLayout.replaceableTracks(
455	    72	                    in: document.editedProject.snapshot, jobs: jobs(in: scope))
456	    73	                : []
457	    74	            plan = try CaptionLayout.place(
458	    75	                result.cues, problems: result.problems, in: document.editedProject,
459	    76	                style: style, looks: looks, replacing: replacing)
460	    77	        } catch {
461	    78	            statusLabel.stringValue = error.localizedDescription
462	    79	            statusLabel.textColor = DS.textStrong
463	    80	            return
464	    81	        }
465	    82	        document.performGroupedEdit("Generate Captions", plan.ops)
466	    83	
467	    84	        // A clean run has nothing to say that the timeline does not already
468	    85	        // show, so it leaves rather than making the user dismiss a receipt.
469	    86	        guard plan.report.isEmpty, cloudLines.isEmpty else {
470	    87	            statusLabel.stringValue =
471	    88	                ([summary(plan), plan.report] + cloudLines)
472	    89	                .filter { !$0.isEmpty }.joined(separator: "\n")
473	    90	            statusLabel.textColor = DS.textStrong
474	    91	            return
475	    92	        }
476	    93	        dismiss(self)
477	    94	    }
478	    95	
479	    96	    /// The media names this sheet opened with, by id — the report card names
480	    97	    /// FILES, because a person chose files and an id is the tool's
481	    98	    /// vocabulary.
482	    99	    private var mediaNames: [UInt32: String] {
483	   100	        var out: [UInt32: String] = [:]
484	   101	        for entry in snapshot.media { out[entry.id] = entry.name }
485	   102	        return out
486	   103	    }
487	   104	
488	   105	    /// The cloud run's extra lines, in a fixed order: R6-8's fallback, the
489	   106	    /// detected language, what is still owed a delete, then any fetched
490	   107	    /// transcript that could not be kept for reuse.
491	   108	    ///
492	   109	    /// The owed list is `Report.deletionWarnings`'s rule: once per media
493	   110	    /// id, because a media can be in `janitorFailed` (an id owed from an
494	   111	    /// earlier run) AND in `uploaded` with `remoteDeleted` false (one owed
495	   112	    /// from this run), and saying it twice would read as two transcripts. A
496	   113	    /// media R6-11 HELD gets one more clause, because "it will be retried"
497	   114	    /// is only half of what happened to it.
498	   115	    static func cloudReportLines(
499	   116	        _ report: CloudTranscriber.Report, names: [UInt32: String], detected: Bool
500	   117	    ) -> [String] {
501	   118	        func name(_ id: UInt32) -> String { names[id] ?? "media \(id)" }
502	   119	        var lines: [String] = []
503	   120	        let preferred = TranscriptOptions.shippedModels.first ?? "universal-3-5-pro"
504	   121	        for row in report.uploaded {
505	   122	            guard let model = row.speechModelUsed, model != preferred else { continue }
506	   123	            lines.append(
507	   124	                "“\(name(row.media))” was transcribed with \(model), not \(preferred).")
508	   125	        }
509	   126	        if detected {
510	   127	            for row in report.uploaded {
511	   128	                guard let code = row.languageCode else { continue }
512	   129	                let spoken = AssemblyAILanguages.entry(code: code)?.displayName ?? code
513	   130	                guard let confidence = row.languageConfidence else {
514	   131	                    lines.append("“\(name(row.media))”: detected \(spoken).")
515	   132	                    continue
516	   133	                }
517	   134	                let percent = Int((min(max(confidence, 0), 1) * 100).rounded())
518	   135	                lines.append(
519	   136	                    "“\(name(row.media))”: detected \(spoken) (\(percent)% confidence).")
520	   137	            }
521	   138	        }
522	   139	        lines.append(contentsOf: report.deletionWarnings { "“\(name($0))”" })
523	   140	        lines.append(contentsOf: report.cacheWarnings { "“\(name($0))”" })
524	   141	        return lines
525	   142	    }
526	   143	
527	   144	    private func summary(_ plan: CaptionLayout.Plan) -> String {
528	   145	        "\(plan.clips) caption\(plan.clips == 1 ? "" : "s") added"
529	   146	            + (plan.trackName.map { " on “\($0)”." } ?? ".")
530	   147	    }
531	   148	
532	   149	    override func viewDidDisappear() {
533	   150	        super.viewDidDisappear()
534	   151	        // A sheet that goes away mid-run must not leave a recognition holding
535	   152	        // a temporary file and somebody's compute.
536	   153	        if didStart, !didFinish { token.cancel() }
537	   154	    }
538	   155	}
539	   156	
540	   157	// MARK: - The menu command
541	   158	
542	   159	/// The command half, at the foot of the file that owns the feature —
543	   160	/// `CaptionImporter.swift`'s precedent, which keeps File ▸ Import Captions…
544	   161	/// beside the importer it opens.
545	   162	extension EditorViewController {
546	   163	
547	   164	    /// File ▸ Generate Captions… — the body of the frozen file's one-line
548	   165	    /// `@objc func generateCaptions(_:)` forward.
549	   166	    ///
550	   167	    /// The refusal happens HERE rather than in the sheet, so a dialog whose
551	   168	    /// only possible answer is "there is nothing with speech in it" never
552	   169	    /// opens — `removeSilencesCommand`'s rule.
553	   170	    func generateCaptionsCommand() {
554	   171	        guard let document = document, view.window?.attachedSheet == nil else {
555	   172	            NSSound.beep()
556	   173	            return
557	   174	        }
558	   175	        guard Transcriber.hasTranscribableClip(in: document.editedProject.snapshot) else {
559	   176	            NSSound.beep()
560	   177	            return
561	   178	        }
562	   179	        // Recognition is minutes of somebody else's compute and the sheet is
563	   180	        // up for all of it; a playhead running under it buys nothing.
564	   181	        playback.pause()

566	   183	    }

     3	/// File ▸ Generate Captions… — road map 2 phase 4a's dialog: a language, a
     4	/// scope, and then the same card turned into a progress bar while
     5	/// `Transcriber` works.
     6	///
     7	/// **One sheet, two states, and that is deliberate.**
     8	/// `ConsolidateProgressSheetController` already changes its own buttons and
     9	/// labels mid-run, and `ExportProgressSheetController` puts the reason best:
    10	/// success and failure both turn the sheet into its own result panel rather
    11	/// than trading it for an alert. Presenting a SECOND sheet from this one's
    12	/// action is the thing `ReverseProgressSheetController.viewDidDisappear`
    13	/// records as not working here — a sheet dismissed a moment ago is still
    14	/// `window.attachedSheet` and the next presentation is refused. Staying one
    15	/// sheet also keeps the bargain that lets this card be trusted: every editor
    16	/// action validates false while a sheet is attached, so the clips it counted
    17	/// in `init` are the clips that will be transcribed.
    18	///
    19	/// **A model is installed HERE and nowhere else** (spec §11 W-8). The
    20	/// Language popup lists every locale the engine supports, a row whose model
    21	/// is missing marked "— not installed", and choosing one shows the Download
    22	/// row (`TranscribeSheetController+Download.swift`): a download is a
    23	/// person's act, so the `transcribe` tool refuses such a locale by name and
    24	/// never downloads. Generate is live only for an installed language. No grant
    25	/// is asked for and no ceiling is reported: W0 q1 measured neither.
    26	///
    27	/// **Two engines, one card (road map 6 §5e).** An Engine popup under
    28	/// Language chooses between the recogniser on this Mac and AssemblyAI, and
    29	/// the choice re-populates Language, shows or hides the three cloud rows, and
    30	/// changes the hint. `TranscribeSheetController+Cloud.swift` holds everything
    31	/// that is only about the cloud engine; what is HERE is the card, and three
    32	/// methods — `refresh`, `noteText` and `startClicked` — whose FIRST statement
    33	/// dispatches on the engine. That order is load-bearing: under
    34	/// `.assemblyai` none of the three reads `language` or `languages`, so a Mac
    35	/// with no on-device model can still transcribe in the cloud.
    36	///
    37	/// **The widenings this split cost**, in toll 3's pattern: `languages`,
    38	/// `mediaURLs`, `languagePopup`, `summaryLabel`, `noteLabel`, `hintLabel`,
    39	/// `scope`, `jobs(in:)`, `startButton`, `showProgress()` and `progressed(_:_:)`
    40	/// are internal rather than private, because `+Cloud.swift` builds the same
    41	/// card out of them. W2 widened `language`, `grid` and `refresh()` for the
    42	/// Download row's file; the cloud half still reads none of them.
    43	///
    44	/// **The Style row and what hangs under it** are two more files:
    45	/// `TranscribeSheetController+Style.swift` (the Style popup, the preview and
    46	/// Replace) and `TranscribeSheetController+Looks.swift` (the three look
    47	/// checkboxes and the on-device note, spec §11 W-15). What is HERE for them
    48	/// is their stored views and their grid rows.
    49	///
    50	/// **Four injection points, for the probe and for nothing else.** `store`,
    51	/// `defaults`, `environment` and `languages` are initialiser arguments with
    52	/// the app's own values as defaults, so an instrument can build this sheet
    53	/// with an empty `MemoryStore`, a throwaway defaults suite, no environment
    54	/// and no on-device model at all, and measure what a person would see.
    55	final class TranscribeSheetController: NSViewController {
    56	
    57	    /// Which clips a run is taken over.
    58	    enum Scope: CaseIterable {
    59	        case selection
    60	        case range
    61	        case all
    62	
    63	        var displayName: String {
    64	            switch self {
    65	            case .selection: return "Selected clips"
    66	            case .range: return "In/out range"
    67	            case .all: return "Whole timeline"
    68	            }
    69	        }
    70	    }
    71	
    72	    /// Weak, like every sheet's back-reference: the document must be free to
    73	    /// close even with a dialog mid-air.

    75	
    76	    /// Everything a run reads, taken off the document once. The document
    77	    /// cannot change under an open sheet, which is what makes that safe.
    78	    let snapshot: ProjectSnapshot
    79	    /// The source maps of the handle `snapshot` came from (spec §11 SR-20 (d)).
    80	    let sourceMaps: SourceMaps
    81	    let mediaURLs: [UInt32: URL]
    82	    private let selection: Set<UInt32>
    83	    private let inOutRange: (start: Ticks, end: Ticks)?
    84	    var languages: [Transcriber.Language]
    85	
    86	    /// Where the AssemblyAI key comes from, where the region and the
    87	    /// remembered engine are read and written, and what a `RC_ASSEMBLYAI_KEY`
    88	    /// would be read out of — injected so a probe can build this card with an
    89	    /// empty store and a throwaway suite. R6-9's folder override is already
    90	    /// inside `AssemblyAIConfiguration.store()`.
    91	    let store: any SecretStore
    92	    let defaults: UserDefaults
    93	    let environment: [String: String]
    94	
    95	    private let transcriber = Transcriber()
    96	    let token = Transcriber.CancelToken()
    97	
    98	    let languagePopup = NSPopUpButton(frame: .zero, pullsDown: false)
    99	    let enginePopup = NSPopUpButton(frame: .zero, pullsDown: false)
   100	    let speakersCheckbox = NSButton(checkboxWithTitle: "", target: nil, action: nil)
   101	    let vocabularyField = NSTextField()
   102	    let refreshCheckbox = NSButton(checkboxWithTitle: "", target: nil, action: nil)
   103	    private let scopePopup = NSPopUpButton(frame: .zero, pullsDown: false)
   104	    let summaryLabel = NSTextField(labelWithString: "")
   105	    let noteLabel = NSTextField(wrappingLabelWithString: "")
   106	    /// The engine's own hint. `makeSheetView` takes `hint: nil` and this
   107	    /// label goes first in the content instead, because the sentence changes
   108	    /// with the popup and the builder's hint is a constructor argument.
   109	    let hintLabel = NSTextField(wrappingLabelWithString: "")
   110	    let bar = NSProgressIndicator()
   111	    let statusLabel = NSTextField(wrappingLabelWithString: "")
   112	    let detailLabel = NSTextField(labelWithString: "")
   113	    let stylePopup = NSPopUpButton(frame: .zero, pullsDown: false)
   114	    /// The three looks (`+Looks.swift`), titled and set by `makeLooksRow()`.
   115	    let slideCheckbox = NSButton(checkboxWithTitle: "", target: nil, action: nil)
   116	    let fillCheckbox = NSButton(checkboxWithTitle: "", target: nil, action: nil)
   117	    let dimCheckbox = NSButton(checkboxWithTitle: "", target: nil, action: nil)
   118	    let dimNoteLabel = NSTextField(wrappingLabelWithString: "")
   119	    let previewView = NSImageView()
   120	    let replaceCheckbox = NSButton(checkboxWithTitle: "existing captions", target: nil, action: nil)
   121	    let replaceLabel = NSTextField(wrappingLabelWithString: "")
   122	    /// Set in `loadView`; the only implicitly-unwrapped optionals here, which
   123	    /// is what app/CLAUDE.md allows them for.
   124	    private var settingsStack: NSStackView!
   125	    private var progressStack: NSStackView!
   126	    var grid: NSGridView!
   127	    var stopButton: NSButton!
   128	    var startButton: NSButton!
   129	    /// The Download row's three views, built by `makeDownloadRow()`.
   130	    var downloadButton: NSButton!
   131	    var downloadBar: NSProgressIndicator!
   132	    var downloadLabel: NSTextField!
   133	    /// The running download's own `Progress`, observed while it runs.
   134	    var downloadProgress: Progress?
   135	    var downloadObservation: NSKeyValueObservation?
   136	    /// The locale the RUNNING download is for; nil when none runs.
   137	    var downloading: Transcriber.Language?
   138	
   139	    /// The run, held for its life: `CloudTranscriber.run` hops onto its own
   140	    /// queue with `[weak self]`, so a transcriber nobody retains never
   141	    /// completes at all.
   142	    var cloud: CloudTranscriber?
   143	    /// What the cloud run said beside its `Outcome` — the report card's
   144	    /// extra lines, read by `finish`.
   145	    var cloudReport: CloudTranscriber.Report?
   146	    /// Whether the language was DETECTED rather than named, which is what
   147	    /// makes a confidence figure a true claim about how it was arrived at.

   482	        showProgress()

   489	                // The run's own queue: every UI touch hops, the way
   490	                // `ConsolidateProgressSheetController` bounces its.
   491	                DispatchQueue.main.async { self?.progressed(fraction, name) }
   492	            },

     5	/// Everything on the Generate Captions card that is only about AssemblyAI —
     6	/// road map 6 §5e. The Language popup's second population, what the controls
     7	/// ADD UP TO (`RunRequest`), the readout the estimate writes, the two hint
     8	/// sentences, the notes, and the run itself.

    10	/// **It is a file of its own for `AgentServer+CloudCaptions.swift`'s reason,
    11	/// read across to the chrome.** The on-device half of this sheet is a story
    12	/// about an installed MODEL and its Download row; this half is a story about a
    13	/// CREDENTIAL, somebody else's money and a cache. Interleaved they read as one
    14	/// tangle, and the main file would be over its cap besides.
    15	///
    16	/// **Nothing here reads the on-device model list, the Download row or `language`.**
    17	/// That is the whole point of the dispatch in the three methods next door: a
    18	/// Mac with no on-device speech model can still transcribe in the cloud, and
    19	/// this file is where that has to stay true.
    20	///
    21	/// **The controls are read in ONE place.** `runRequest()` is the function
    22	/// from the card's state to what a run would receive, and everything else —
    23	/// the estimate, the notes, the button, the run — goes through it, so the
    24	/// summary can never describe a different request from the one Generate
    25	/// sends. The vocabulary's rules are `TranscriptOptions.keyterms`, the same
    26	/// function the tool uses and not a second copy of it.

   115	
   116	    /// The card's state as what a run would be given — one value, so the
   117	    /// readout, the notes, the button and Generate itself cannot disagree.
   118	    struct RunRequest: Equatable {
   119	        let engine: TranscriptionEngine
   120	        /// The on-device locale identifier, and nil for the cloud engine.
   121	        let appleLanguage: String?
   122	        /// The cloud request, and nil for the on-device engine.
   123	        let options: TranscriptOptions?
   124	        let refresh: Bool
   125	        /// How many terms were TYPED, before the trim, the de-duplication and
   126	        /// the cap — `capNote` is the only reader.
   127	        let vocabularyGiven: Int
   128	    }
   129	
   130	    func runRequest() -> RunRequest {
   131	        let chosen = engine
   132	        guard chosen == .assemblyai else {
   133	            return RunRequest(
   134	                engine: .apple, appleLanguage: languagePopup.selectedItem?.representedObject
   135	                    as? String, options: nil, refresh: false, vocabularyGiven: 0)
   136	        }
   137	        let vocabulary = Self.vocabulary(from: vocabularyField.stringValue)
   138	        let code = languagePopup.selectedItem?.representedObject as? String
   139	        return RunRequest(
   140	            engine: .assemblyai, appleLanguage: nil,
   141	            options: TranscriptOptions(
   142	                speechModels: TranscriptOptions.shippedModels,
   143	                languageCode: (code?.isEmpty ?? true) ? nil : code,
   144	                speakerLabels: speakersCheckbox.state == .on,
   145	                keytermsPrompt: vocabulary.terms),
   146	            refresh: refreshCheckbox.state == .on, vocabularyGiven: vocabulary.given)
   147	    }
   148	
   149	    /// The Vocabulary field as the tool's `vocabulary` argument: split on
   150	    /// commas, then `TranscriptOptions.keyterms` — the SAME trim, the same
   151	    /// de-duplication keeping the first spelling, the same cap. `given` is
   152	    /// the count before any of that, which is what the tool's own note says.
   153	    static func vocabulary(from text: String) -> (given: Int, terms: [String]) {
   154	        guard !text.trimmingCharacters(in: .whitespacesAndNewlines).isEmpty else {
   155	            return (0, [])
   156	        }
   157	        let pieces = text.split(separator: ",", omittingEmptySubsequences: false).map(String.init)
   158	        return (pieces.count, TranscriptOptions.keyterms(pieces))
   159	    }

712	   270	    /// through the active word's pop, nil for none), with the three looks of
713	   271	    /// spec §11 W-14: `glide` (0…1 through the pill's slide from token
714	   272	    /// `word − 2`), `fill` (0…1 of the active word filled) and `dim` (0…1
715	   273	    /// into a pause's dim, nil for a page whose dim is not this bitmap's).
716	   274	    /// All three are clamped — `glide` and `fill` here, `dim` and `pauseDim`
717	   275	    /// in `dimAmount`: an action's end patch is not range-checked.
718	   276	    ///
719	   277	    /// **With `activePill.glide` not set and `fill` and `dim` nil, the calls
720	   278	    /// are the ones this routine has always made, in their order.** The base
721	   279	    /// pass first, token by token: build mode skips the upcoming tokens
722	   280	    /// (`≥ word`), highlight draws them in `upcoming_color` when set; the
723	   281	    /// spoken ones (`< word − 1`) take `spoken_color` when set; the base
724	   282	    /// colour otherwise. Then the ACTIVE token, `word − 1`, in this order
725	   283	    /// inside one saved state: the CTM scaled about its pill's centre by
726	   284	    /// `1 + (active_scale − 1) × backOut(pop)`; the pill filled UNCLIPPED —
727	   285	    /// it reaches past the midpoints by design; then the midpoint clip, set

729	   287	    /// `active_color`. Clipping before scaling would shave the popped
730	   288	    /// word's end glyphs at the unscaled midpoints.
731	   289	    ///

733	   291	    /// the page**, sliding or settled, so every word's ink lies over it —
734	   292	    /// the word it is leaving included — and the order never flips when a
735	   293	    /// slide ends. Its rect is the interpolation of token `word − 2`'s pill
736	   294	    /// and the active token's at `easeOut(glide)` when each lies on one
737	   295	    /// line, else the active token's settled pill; it pops about its OWN
738	   296	    /// centre, and the active token still pops about its settled pill's.
739	   297	    ///

741	   299	    /// token's glyph range, on a whole device pixel; the active ink left of
742	   300	    /// it, and right of it the upcoming ink (highlight) or nothing (build).

745	   303	    ///

747	   305	    /// `1 − dimAmount(dim, pauseDim:)`, drawn HERE — which only a page with a

750	   308	    /// drawn undimmed and the whole bitmap multiplied once
751	   309	    /// (`scaleBitmap`), on every exit after drawing starts, so the context
752	   310	    /// must hold nothing but this page when a dim is passed; a context with
753	   311	    /// no memory, decided before anything is drawn, takes one transparency
754	   312	    /// layer instead. For a page with no backdrop the caller hands a nil
755	   313	    /// `dim`, this routine draws the undimmed page, and the compositor
756	   314	    /// multiplies the layer's opacity (`wordDim(of:reveal:)`, spec §11 W-16).
757	   315	    static func drawWords(
758	   316	        _ layout: TextLayout, of props: TextProps, style: WordStyle, word: Int, pop: Double?,

770	   328	        }
771	   329	        defer {

796	   354	                glide: glide, size: size, scale: scale, in: context)
797	   355	        }
798	   356	        drawBase(
799	   357	            layout, tokens, word: word, mode: style.mode, spoken: spoken, upcoming: upcoming,
800	   358	            in: context)
801	   359	
802	   360	        guard active >= 0, active < tokens.count else { return }
803	   361	        let activeInk = style.activeColor.map { ink(props, $0) } ?? base
804	   362	        let filled: Double? = fill.map { min(max($0, 0), 1) }

816	   374	                fillPlate(plate, in: pill, size: size, in: context)
817	   375	            }

819	   377	            // the fill's edge when it is filling.

825	   383	                        in: context)

828	   386	                    in: context)

830	   388	                    drawToken(

832	   390	                        height: height, in: context)

838	   396	            }

844	   402	    /// `easeOut(glide)` while it slides and each is one piece, else on
845	   403	    /// `to`'s pieces, settled. A nil `glide` is a page's first word, or a
846	   404	    /// caller with no recipe (the sheet's preview): settled.

849	   407	        scale: CGFloat, in context: CGContext
850	   408	    ) {

1	     1	//! The word-caption vocabulary (format version 9, road map 8's W1b):
2	     2	//! [`TextCase`], the [`Word`] timings a caption page carries, and the
3	     3	//! [`WordStyle`] (with its [`WordMode`] and [`ActivePill`]) that says how
4	     4	//! the word being spoken is drawn — plus the two small facts every writer
5	     5	//! of `text.words` shares, [`token_count`] and [`rebase_words`]. Format
6	     6	//! version 12 (spec §11, W-12) added three looks as KEYS, each off by
7	     7	//! default: [`ActivePill::glide`], [`WordStyle::active_fill`] and
8	     8	//! [`WordStyle::pause_dim`].
9	     9	//!
10	    10	//! **A word caption is an ordinary text clip holding one PAGE** (spec §11,
11	    11	//! W-1): `content` is the page, `words` is one `{start, end}` per
12	    12	//! whitespace token of it, in CLIP time, and `word_style` is how the
13	    13	//! renderer shows which of them has been said. Nothing here is a measured
14	    14	//! size or a per-frame answer — `recipe_words.rs` computes the five word
15	    15	//! keys (`word`, `word_pop`, `word_glide`, `word_fill`, `word_dim`) from
16	    16	//! these at render time and stores nothing — which is the seam `model_text.rs` states for the text group as a whole, read once
17	    17	//! more: the model says what the words ARE and when they are said, and only
18	    18	//! the platform knows where each one lands on the page.
19	    19	//!
20	    20	//! **The core is the one counter** (W-2). [`token_count`] is
21	    21	//! `str::split_whitespace`, the rule road map 8's W0 q4 measured against the
22	    22	//! renderer's own tokenizer over a corpus written to make them differ, and
23	    23	//! they agree on the COUNT in every row — the only number `check_text`
24	    24	//! reads. **Word times move with the content, not with the clip's length**
25	    25	//! (W-3): [`rebase_words`] is the one subtraction `trim_start`, `roll`,
26	    26	//! `add_transition`'s handle form and `split`'s second half each make, and
27	    27	//! nothing rescales them.
28	    28	//!
29	    29	//! Re-exported whole by `model_props.rs`, which `model.rs` re-exports whole
30	    30	//! in turn, so `crate::model::WordStyle` resolves like every other property
31	    31	//! type; the FIELDS holding these (`TextProps.case`, `.words`,
32	    32	//! `.word_style`) stay with the text group. The two functions are
33	    33	//! `pub(crate)`, and a glob re-export cannot widen them, so their callers
34	    34	//! name `crate::model_words` directly.
35	    35	//!
36	    36	//! No enum's declaration ORDER is load-bearing — nothing derives a number
37	    37	//! from it — so a value may be added at the END (W-4). The JSON spelling of
38	    38	//! each variant IS persisted, so a rename needs a migration step. The rules
39	    39	//! are `model.rs`'s: the field names ARE the JSON keys, declaration order IS
40	    40	//! key order, every struct is `#[serde(default)]` over a [`Default`] that
41	    41	//! says what an absent key means, and nothing here carries
42	    42	//! `deny_unknown_fields`.

52	    52	#[derive(Debug, Clone, Copy, Default, PartialEq, Eq, Serialize, Deserialize)]

58	    58	    Upper,

64	    64	/// the second half's words by the cut, so a split page is invisible. Two

118	   118	#[derive(Debug, Clone, Copy, PartialEq, Serialize, Deserialize)]

133	   133	    pub active_fill: bool,

136	   136	    pub pause_dim: f64,
137	   137	}

140	   140	    fn default() -> Self {
141	   141	        WordStyle {
142	   142	            mode: WordMode::Highlight,
143	   143	            active_color: None,
144	   144	            active_scale: 1.0,
145	   145	            active_pill: None,
146	   146	            spoken_color: None,
147	   147	            upcoming_color: None,
148	   148	            active_fill: false,

151	   151	    }
152	   152	}

154	   154	impl WordStyle {
155	   155	    /// Every slot filled with its default.
156	   156	    ///
157	   157	    /// Not a value any clip is given: this is what `patch.rs`'s text
158	   158	    /// template holds so the key walk knows the kind of every member an
159	   159	    /// optional slot can carry, which a `None` could not tell it.
160	   160	    pub fn template() -> WordStyle {
161	   161	        WordStyle {
162	   162	            mode: WordMode::Highlight,
163	   163	            active_color: Some([1.0, 1.0, 1.0, 1.0]),
164	   164	            active_scale: 1.0,
165	   165	            active_pill: Some(ActivePill::default()),
166	   166	            spoken_color: Some([1.0, 1.0, 1.0, 1.0]),
167	   167	            upcoming_color: Some([1.0, 1.0, 1.0, 1.0]),
168	   168	            active_fill: false,
169	   169	            pause_dim: 0.0,
170	   170	        }
171	   171	    }
172	   172	}
173	   173

614	   172	    private static func ink(_ props: TextProps, _ color: RGBA) -> WordInk {
615	   173	        let alpha = color.count > 3 ? min(max(color[3], 0), 1) : 1

617	   175	        if opaque.count > 3 { opaque[3] = 1 }

621	   179	    /// Draws one line of `ink` at its alpha, clipped to `left…right`.
622	   180	    private static func drawToken(

624	   182	        in context: CGContext

628	   186	            ink.layout.lines[index], alpha: ink.alpha, left: left, right: right, height: height,

632	   190	    /// `1 − (1 − u)³`, the curve a gliding pill rides: fast off the word it
633	   191	    /// leaves, settling onto the active one (spec §11 W-14).
634	   192	    static func easeOut(_ u: Double) -> Double {
635	   193	        let p = 1 - u
636	   194	        return 1 - p * p * p
637	   195	    }
638	   196	
639	   197	    /// The part of one token that lies on one line: where its glyph range
640	   198	    /// starts and ends, the pill around it, and its midpoint clip.
641	   199	    private struct TokenPiece {
642	   200	        let line: Int
643	   201	        let left: CGFloat
644	   202	        let right: CGFloat
645	   203	        let pill: CGRect
646	   204	        let bounds: (left: CGFloat, right: CGFloat)
647	   205	    }

649	   207	    /// `token`'s pieces in line order — one, unless the token wraps; none
650	   208	    /// for an index that is no token.
651	   209	    private static func pieces(
652	   210	        of token: Int, _ layout: TextLayout, _ tokens: [Range<Int>], pad: CGFloat
653	   211	    ) -> [TokenPiece] {
654	   212	        guard tokens.indices.contains(token) else { return [] }
655	   213	        var found: [TokenPiece] = []
656	   214	        for (index, laid) in layout.lines.enumerated() {
657	   215	            let line = laid.range.location..<(laid.range.location + laid.range.length)
658	   216	            let here = tokensOnLine(tokens, line)
659	   217	            guard let position = here.firstIndex(of: token) else { continue }
660	   218	            let range = tokens[token].clamped(to: line)
661	   219	            let left = laid.origin.x
662	   220	                + CTLineGetOffsetForStringIndex(laid.line, range.lowerBound, nil)
663	   221	            let right = laid.origin.x
664	   222	                + CTLineGetOffsetForStringIndex(laid.line, range.upperBound, nil)
665	   223	            let pill = CGRect(
666	   224	                x: left - pad, y: laid.origin.y - laid.descent - pad,
667	   225	                width: (right - left) + pad * 2, height: laid.ascent + laid.descent + pad * 2)
668	   226	            found.append(
669	   227	                TokenPiece(
670	   228	                    line: index, left: left, right: right, pill: pill,
671	   229	                    bounds: clipBounds(layout, laid, tokens, here, position, line)))
672	   230	        }

674	   232	    }
675	   233	
676	   234	    /// Fills `plate` in `rect`, scaled about the rect's own centre.
677	   235	    private static func fillPlate(
678	   236	        _ plate: ActivePill, in rect: CGRect, size: CGFloat, scale: CGFloat, in context: CGContext
679	   237	    ) {
680	   238	        context.saveGState()
681	   239	        context.translateBy(x: rect.midX, y: rect.midY)
682	   240	        context.scaleBy(x: scale, y: scale)
683	   241	        context.translateBy(x: -rect.midX, y: -rect.midY)
684	   242	        fillPlate(plate, in: rect, size: size, in: context)
685	   243	        context.restoreGState()
686	   244	    }

688	   246	    private static func fillPlate(
689	   247	        _ plate: ActivePill, in rect: CGRect, size: CGFloat, in context: CGContext
690	   248	    ) {
691	   249	        guard rect.width > 0, rect.height > 0 else { return }
692	   250	        let radius = min(CGFloat(plate.radius) * size, min(rect.width, rect.height) / 2)
693	   251	        context.addPath(
694	   252	            CGPath(
695	   253	                roundedRect: rect, cornerWidth: max(radius, 0), cornerHeight: max(radius, 0),
696	   254	                transform: nil))

698	   256	        context.fillPath()
699	   257	    }

701	   259	    /// `x` moved onto the nearest whole DEVICE pixel column under the
702	   260	    /// context's current transform, so a fill's edge never antialiases.
703	   261	    private static func snappedToDevice(
704	   262	        _ x: CGFloat, y: CGFloat, in context: CGContext
705	   263	    ) -> CGFloat {
706	   264	        var device = context.convertToDeviceSpace(CGPoint(x: x, y: y))
707	   265	        device.x = device.x.rounded()
708	   266	        return context.convertToUserSpace(device).x
709	   267	    }
710	   268	
711	   269	    /// A timed page at `word` (how many words have started) and `pop` (0…1
712	   270	    /// through the active word's pop, nil for none), with the three looks of
713	   271	    /// spec §11 W-14: `glide` (0…1 through the pill's slide from token
714	   272	    /// `word − 2`), `fill` (0…1 of the active word filled) and `dim` (0…1
715	   273	    /// into a pause's dim, nil for a page whose dim is not this bitmap's).
716	   274	    /// All three are clamped — `glide` and `fill` here, `dim` and `pauseDim`
717	   275	    /// in `dimAmount`: an action's end patch is not range-checked.
718	   276	    ///
719	   277	    /// **With `activePill.glide` not set and `fill` and `dim` nil, the calls
720	   278	    /// are the ones this routine has always made, in their order.** The base
721	   279	    /// pass first, token by token: build mode skips the upcoming tokens
722	   280	    /// (`≥ word`), highlight draws them in `upcoming_color` when set; the
723	   281	    /// spoken ones (`< word − 1`) take `spoken_color` when set; the base
724	   282	    /// colour otherwise. Then the ACTIVE token, `word − 1`, in this order
725	   283	    /// inside one saved state: the CTM scaled about its pill's centre by
726	   284	    /// `1 + (active_scale − 1) × backOut(pop)`; the pill filled UNCLIPPED —
727	   285	    /// it reaches past the midpoints by design; then the midpoint clip, set
728	   286	    /// in text space so the CTM scales it with the token, and the token in
729	   287	    /// `active_color`. Clipping before scaling would shave the popped
730	   288	    /// word's end glyphs at the unscaled midpoints.
731	   289	    ///
732	   290	    /// **A gliding pill is filled BEFORE the base pass, in every frame of
733	   291	    /// the page**, sliding or settled, so every word's ink lies over it —
734	   292	    /// the word it is leaving included — and the order never flips when a
735	   293	    /// slide ends. Its rect is the interpolation of token `word − 2`'s pill
736	   294	    /// and the active token's at `easeOut(glide)` when each lies on one
737	   295	    /// line, else the active token's settled pill; it pops about its OWN
738	   296	    /// centre, and the active token still pops about its settled pill's.
739	   297	    ///
740	   298	    /// **A fill's edge is hard**: `left + fill × (right − left)` over the
741	   299	    /// token's glyph range, on a whole device pixel; the active ink left of
742	   300	    /// it, and right of it the upcoming ink (highlight) or nothing (build).
743	   301	    /// At 1 the edge is the token's own clip bound, so a full word is drawn
744	   302	    /// whole — an outline's stroke reaches past the glyph range.
745	   303	    ///
746	   304	    /// **A dim is one opacity over the words and the pill together**,
747	   305	    /// `1 − dimAmount(dim, pauseDim:)`, drawn HERE — which only a page with a
748	   306	    /// backdrop asks for, and its caller puts the backdrop under the words
749	   307	    /// AFTER this returns, so it never dims (spec §11 W-17). The page is
750	   308	    /// drawn undimmed and the whole bitmap multiplied once
751	   309	    /// (`scaleBitmap`), on every exit after drawing starts, so the context
752	   310	    /// must hold nothing but this page when a dim is passed; a context with
753	   311	    /// no memory, decided before anything is drawn, takes one transparency
754	   312	    /// layer instead. For a page with no backdrop the caller hands a nil
755	   313	    /// `dim`, this routine draws the undimmed page, and the compositor
756	   314	    /// multiplies the layer's opacity (`wordDim(of:reveal:)`, spec §11 W-16).
757	   315	    static func drawWords(
758	   316	        _ layout: TextLayout, of props: TextProps, style: WordStyle, word: Int, pop: Double?,
759	   317	        glide: Double? = nil, fill: Double? = nil, dim: Double? = nil, in context: CGContext
760	   318	    ) {
761	   319	        let tokens = tokens(of: props.laidContent)
762	   320	        guard !tokens.isEmpty, !layout.lines.isEmpty else { return }
763	   321	        let dimmed = dimAmount(dim, pauseDim: style.pauseDim)
764	   322	        guard dimmed < 1 else { return }
765	   323	        let multiplies = dimmed > 0 && context.data != nil
766	   324	        if dimmed > 0, !multiplies {
767	   325	            context.saveGState()
768	   326	            context.setAlpha(CGFloat(1 - dimmed))
769	   327	            context.beginTransparencyLayer(auxiliaryInfo: nil)
770	   328	        }
771	   329	        defer {
772	   330	            if multiplies {
773	   331	                scaleBitmap(context, by: 1 - dimmed)
774	   332	            } else if dimmed > 0 {
775	   333	                context.endTransparencyLayer()
776	   334	                context.restoreGState()
777	   335	            }
778	   336	        }
779	   337	        context.textMatrix = .identity
780	   338	        // The base colour draws from the layout AS LAID, as the static page
781	   339	        // does: fill at its own alpha, the stroke at the outline's.
782	   340	        let base = WordInk(layout: layout, alpha: 1)
783	   341	        let spoken = style.spokenColor.map { ink(props, $0) } ?? base
784	   342	        let upcoming = style.upcomingColor.map { ink(props, $0) } ?? base
785	   343	        let active = word - 1
786	   344	        let height = layout.size.height
787	   345	        let size = max(1, CGFloat(props.size))
788	   346	        let scale = pop.map { 1 + CGFloat(style.activeScale - 1) * CGFloat(backOut($0)) } ?? 1
789	   347	        let pad = CGFloat(style.activePill?.padding ?? 0) * size
790	   348	        let activePieces = pieces(of: active, layout, tokens, pad: pad)
791	   349	        let glidingPlate = style.activePill.flatMap { $0.glide ? $0 : nil }
792	   350	
793	   351	        if let plate = glidingPlate {
794	   352	            drawGlidingPlate(
795	   353	                plate, to: activePieces, from: pieces(of: active - 1, layout, tokens, pad: pad),
796	   354	                glide: glide, size: size, scale: scale, in: context)
797	   355	        }
798	   356	        drawBase(
799	   357	            layout, tokens, word: word, mode: style.mode, spoken: spoken, upcoming: upcoming,
800	   358	            in: context)
801	   359	
802	   360	        guard active >= 0, active < tokens.count else { return }
803	   361	        let activeInk = style.activeColor.map { ink(props, $0) } ?? base
804	   362	        let filled: Double? = fill.map { min(max($0, 0), 1) }
805	   363	        for piece in activePieces {
806	   364	            let pill = piece.pill
807	   365	            let bounds = piece.bounds
808	   366	            context.saveGState()
809	   367	            // (a) the pop, about the pill's centre.
810	   368	            context.translateBy(x: pill.midX, y: pill.midY)
811	   369	            context.scaleBy(x: scale, y: scale)
812	   370	            context.translateBy(x: -pill.midX, y: -pill.midY)
813	   371	            // (b) the pill, unclipped — unless it glides, and is already
814	   372	            // down under the base pass.
815	   373	            if glidingPlate == nil, let plate = style.activePill {
816	   374	                fillPlate(plate, in: pill, size: size, in: context)
817	   375	            }
818	   376	            // (c) the token, clipped at its midpoints in text space, and at
819	   377	            // the fill's edge when it is filling.
820	   378	            if let filled {
821	   379	                let edge = filled >= 1
822	   380	                    ? bounds.right
823	   381	                    : snappedToDevice(
824	   382	                        piece.left + CGFloat(filled) * (piece.right - piece.left), y: pill.midY,
825	   383	                        in: context)

827	   385	                    activeInk, line: piece.line, left: bounds.left, right: edge, height: height,
828	   386	                    in: context)
829	   387	                if style.mode == .highlight, edge < bounds.right {
830	   388	                    drawToken(
831	   389	                        upcoming, line: piece.line, left: edge, right: bounds.right,
832	   390	                        height: height, in: context)
833	   391	                }
834	   392	            } else {
835	   393	                drawToken(
836	   394	                    activeInk, line: piece.line, left: bounds.left, right: bounds.right,
837	   395	                    height: height, in: context)
838	   396	            }
839	   397	            context.restoreGState()
840	   398	        }
841	   399	    }
842	   400	
843	   401	    /// A gliding pill's plate: between `from`'s pill and `to`'s at
844	   402	    /// `easeOut(glide)` while it slides and each is one piece, else on
845	   403	    /// `to`'s pieces, settled. A nil `glide` is a page's first word, or a
846	   404	    /// caller with no recipe (the sheet's preview): settled.
847	   405	    private static func drawGlidingPlate(
848	   406	        _ plate: ActivePill, to: [TokenPiece], from: [TokenPiece], glide: Double?, size: CGFloat,
849	   407	        scale: CGFloat, in context: CGContext
850	   408	    ) {
851	   409	        var rects = to.map { $0.pill }
852	   410	        let travel = CGFloat(easeOut(min(max(glide ?? 1, 0), 1)))
853	   411	        if travel < 1, to.count == 1, from.count == 1 {
854	   412	            let a = from[0].pill
855	   413	            let b = to[0].pill
856	   414	            rects = [
857	   415	                CGRect(
858	   416	                    x: a.minX + (b.minX - a.minX) * travel,
859	   417	                    y: a.minY + (b.minY - a.minY) * travel,
860	   418	                    width: a.width + (b.width - a.width) * travel,
861	   419	                    height: a.height + (b.height - a.height) * travel)
862	   420	            ]
863	   421	        }
864	   422	        for rect in rects {
865	   423	            fillPlate(plate, in: rect, size: size, scale: scale, in: context)
866	   424	        }
867	   425	    }
868	   426	
869	   427	    /// The base pass: every token but the active one, `word − 1`.
870	   428	    private static func drawBase(
871	   429	        _ layout: TextLayout, _ tokens: [Range<Int>], word: Int, mode: WordMode, spoken: WordInk,
872	   430	        upcoming: WordInk, in context: CGContext
873	   431	    ) {
874	   432	        let active = word - 1
875	   433	        let height = layout.size.height
876	   434	        for (index, laid) in layout.lines.enumerated() {
877	   435	            let line = laid.range.location..<(laid.range.location + laid.range.length)
878	   436	            // `tokensOnLine`: the tokens with ink on THIS line.
879	   437	            let here = tokensOnLine(tokens, line)
880	   438	            for (position, token) in here.enumerated() where token != active {
881	   439	                if token >= word, mode == .build { continue }
882	   440	                let bounds = clipBounds(layout, laid, tokens, here, position, line)
883	   441	                drawToken(
884	   442	                    token >= word ? upcoming : spoken, line: index, left: bounds.left,
885	   443	                    right: bounds.right, height: height, in: context)
886	   444	            }
887	   445	        }
888	   446	    }

    13	/// bound on `Job.sourceIn`, the clamp inside `contentLength(of:)` and
    14	/// `placed(offset:in:)`, the one door every `Double → Ticks` conversion on
    15	/// the caption path goes through. One widening survives from the move:
    16	/// `contentLength(of:)` is internal rather than `private` (road map 6 §5h
    17	/// names it), which no compiler error demanded — its one caller, `jobs`,
    18	/// moved with it.
    19	///
    20	/// **Why anything here is bounded at all — spec §11's R6-10.** A clip's
    21	/// `speed` is bounded to `SPEED_MIN`/`SPEED_MAX` by the OPS
    22	/// (`core/src/edit_clip_timing.rs`: `set_speed` clamps, `rate_stretch` is an
    23	/// identity outside) and, since R6-10's amendment (#41), by the reader too
    24	/// — `Project::validate`'s `check_clips` refuses a clip outside them — so
    25	/// no opened project reaches this code with a tiny or huge speed. The
    26	/// clamps here stay as the second layer R6-10 keeps, because if one ever
    27	/// did, the two ends of the arithmetic would fail in two places: a huge
    28	/// speed overflows the SOURCE LENGTH here, and a tiny one overflows the
    29	/// OFFSET in the two mappings. Both clamp in `Double`, before the
    30	/// conversion, because a `Ticks(_:)` on an out-of-range `Double` traps.
    31	extension Transcriber {
    32	
    33	    /// The ceiling on any source time this file answers: 1e15 ticks, about
    34	    /// 1.9 billion seconds, some fifty years of media.
    35	    ///
    36	    /// Deliberately NOT `Ticks.max`, which is what the core's own
    37	    /// `content_length_in_source` saturates at (`core/src/source_window.rs`
    38	    /// casts an `f64` and an out-of-range cast saturates in Rust rather than
    39	    /// trapping). The core never ADDS that number to anything; Swift does.
    40	    /// `MediaTranscript.words` adds it to `sourceIn` for the window's end,
    41	    /// and `TranscribeSheetController.refresh` sums it over every job, at
    42	    /// most `MAX_CLIPS` = 4096 of them — and 4096 × 1e15 is under 2^63 with
    43	    /// three orders of magnitude to spare, where 4096 × `Ticks.max` is not.
    44	    static let maxSourceTicks: Ticks = 1_000_000_000_000_000
    45	
    46	    /// One offset in ticks, as a `Double`, landed in the clip — the ONE
    47	    /// door both caption mappings convert through.
    48	    ///
    49	    /// The clamp is into `[0, duration]` and it happens in `Double`: an
    50	    /// offset divided by a speed of 1e-300 is a finite `Double` far larger
    51	    /// than `Ticks.max`, and `Ticks(_:)` on it traps rather than saturating.
    52	    /// Rounded half away from zero, the rule both mappings had. NaN — which
    53	    /// is what `0 / 0` answers when a word sits exactly on a zero-speed
    54	    /// clip's `in` point — is 0, the clip's own start: the beginning of the
    55	    /// clip is the one answer that is always inside it.
    56	    static func placed(offset: Double, in job: Job) -> Ticks {
    57	        guard !offset.isNaN else { return job.start }
    58	        let bounded = min(max(offset, 0), Double(job.duration))
    59	        return job.start + Ticks(bounded.rounded(.toNearestOrAwayFromZero))
    60	    }
